subject: Hyperion model p95 latency variance — request for SLA exception & mitigation plan
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya@optechtics.com>
Cc: Alex Romero <alex.romero@optechtics.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Jul 2026 08:15:22 -0700
Subject: Hyperion model p95 latency variance — detected increase

Hi Maya / Alex,

Quick note from the infra runbook — our monitoring started to show a sustained increase in p95 latency for hyperion-v2.4 serving your production route (optechtics-recommend) starting ~2026-07-02 22:00 UTC. The impact: p95 has moved from our 220ms SLA bucket to ~540ms over the last 18 hours for queries with avg tokens ~48. We've attached the p95 report and a small trace bundle.

We want to be transparent and propose these immediate actions:
- Short term: route traffic to hyperion-v2.2 (a compatible variant with identical semantics) while we investigate root cause. This would be a rollback at the model-version level (v2.4 -> v2.2) and is expected to restore p95 to ~200–250ms.
- Medium term: collect KV cache traces and sequence-length distribution to determine whether the degradation is due to batching/kv-caching interaction.
- We'll prepare an RCA and timeline by EOD Monday.

Before we proceed with any rollback we need confirmation from your side that a temporary model switch is acceptable from a correctness/QA standpoint. If we don't hear back in 2 business hours we'll escalate internally for a forced fallback to preserve SLAs.

Attachments: 2026-07-03_hyperion_p95_report.csv; kv-cache-traces-20260703.zip

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
From: Maya Singh <maya@optechtics.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Romero <alex.romero@optechtics.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Jul 2026 08:42:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Hyperion model p95 latency variance — detected increase

Thanks for the heads up, Rishi.

Can you confirm: will the rollback change any response formatting or ranking behavior? We run a small post-process that depends on a tokenization quirk that was introduced in v2.4 — if responses differ it may break our pipeline.

If the switch is a pure performance/implementation fallback with no semantic deltas, we are fine to proceed; otherwise we need a short eval run (1000 queries) before you flip traffic.

Also looping in Procurement because this may affect our SLA credits/uptime reporting.

— Maya
Director, Product & Integrations
Maya Singh, Optechtics
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya@optechtics.com>, Alex Romero <alex.romero@optechtics.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Jul 2026 09:05:33 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Hyperion model p95 latency variance — detected increase

Laura / Marissa — FYI and need a quick decision. Maya flagged potential semantic delta due to tokenization quirk in v2.4 (their post-process). They asked for a 1k-query eval before we roll.

Options:
1) Run a 1k eval against v2.2 in prod-shared (shadow) within 30 mins, share diff report, then flip. This will add ~45–60 minutes to mitigation but avoids breaking their post-processing.
2) Perform immediate rollback (auto-fallback) to guarantee SLA numbers and then perform a targeted compatibility pass; risk: may surface small downstream breakages for Optechtics.

We also have the route-level canary policy: auto-fallback if p95 > 400ms for >1 hour. We're at ~540ms now and climbing.

Recommendation: do (1) — run the 1k eval in shadow. I'm starting trace collection and can push a pre-approved rollback_signoff PDF if we need fast approval.

-Rishi

Thanks for the context — and good catch by monitoring. A few clarifying items before we run the eval:
- Marissa: can ops produce a 1k eval harness that mirrors Optechtics' production tokenization/post-process? If we can simulate the post-process quickly we reduce risk.
- Rishi: capture the exact time ranges and input distribution for the p95 spike (attach to the HubSpot deal).

Operational decision: run the 1k shadow eval now. If the diff report shows <0.5% semantic divergence on our canonical metrics (BLEU/semantic-sim), we approve the rollback and will execute a controlled traffic shift (10% increments over 10 minutes). If the divergence is >0.5%, pause and set up a joint debug session.

I've uploaded a one-click signoff PDF for expedited approval if all checks pass (attached).

-Laura
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya@optechtics.com>, Optechtics Procurement <procurement@optechtics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Jul 2026 14:02:10 -0700
Subject: Hyperion mitigation update — 1k eval completed; controlled rollback executed

Maya / team — final update:

- We ran the 1,000-query shadow evaluation against hyperion-v2.2 using Optechtics' sample set and a simulated post-process. Results: semantic divergence 0.18% on our canonical metric set (well under the 0.5% threshold). Detailed CSV attached.
- Controlled rollback from v2.4 -> v2.2 performed at 2026-07-07 20:45 UTC using 10% traffic increments over 12 minutes. Post-rollback p95 is 230ms (rolling 10m window).
- We've attached the final p95 CSV and the kv-cache trace bundle we used for the RCA.
- We've created an incident record and a short RCA (link above) — root cause appears to be an interaction between a sparse attention kernel path in v2.4 and our continuous-batching adjustments for your traffic distribution; final fix will be in v2.4.1.

Next steps:
1) We'll track any downstream post-process regressions over the next 48 hours. Please surface anything unexpected.
2) Engineering will release v2.4.1 candidate in 10 days; we'll schedule a coordinated upgrade with a canary plan.
3) Procurement / Finance: we'll follow the SLA credits process per the agreement — Rishi, please open the credit request in HubSpot (deal OP-2026-1729).

Attachments: rollback_signoff_hyperion_v2.3_to_v2.2.pdf; 2026-07-03_hyperion_p95_report.csv; kv-cache-traces-20260703.zip

Thanks for the quick coordination — appreciate the patience.

-Rishi
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
